responsibility: This module provides GCC’s shared operating-system and environment configuration layer outside individual CPU back ends. It defines reusable target headers, option tables, and helper implementations that describe how GCC should behave for major host and target OS families such as Darwin, Linux/Android, Solaris, the BSDs, VxWorks, RTEMS, Fuchsia, Hurd/GNU, and related environments. Across these file groups it covers OS-specific preprocessor builtins, ABI and <stdint.h> type models, linker/startfile/endfile and dynamic-linker specs, assembler/debug-format conventions, target and driver option metadata, language-frontend OS hooks for C-family, D, and Rust, object-format support such as ELF or Mach-O section policy, and small compatibility shims like builtin patching or libc capability queries. It also includes host-side support code such as precompiled-header mapping hooks and build-time helpers like sysroot-suffix generation. In short, gcc/config/root is the common repository for machine-independent or cross-target OS, runtime, toolchain, and driver configuration logic that neighboring architecture-specific gcc/config/<arch> modules build on.
